what_its_for: Rivastigmine is used to treat mild to moderate dementia (memory loss and confusion) caused by Alzheimer's disease or Parkinson's disease. It does not cure these conditions, but it can help improve memory, thinking, and daily functioning.
how_to_take: Rivastigmine comes as a capsule, liquid solution, or skin patch. Take capsules or liquid WITH food (breakfast and dinner) to reduce stomach upset. For the patch: apply it to clean, dry, hairless skin on your upper back, upper arm, or chest. Press firmly for 30 seconds. Change the patch every 24 hours and rotate the site each time — do not put a new patch on the same spot for at least 14 days. Never wear more than one patch at a time. Swallow capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. For the liquid, use the measuring syringe provided and mix it into water, juice, or cold soda if desired.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to reduce side effects. Capsules usually start at 1.5 mg twice daily and may be increased up to 6 mg twice daily. The patch usually starts at 4.6 mg per 24 hours and may be increased to 9.5 mg or 13.3 mg per 24 hours. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the capsule or liquid, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double up to make up for a missed dose. If you miss more than 3 days of doses for any reason, contact your doctor before restarting — your dose may need to be lowered again to avoid serious side effects.
storage: Store capsules and liquid at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the liquid bottle upright. Do not freeze the liquid. Store patches at room temperature and keep them in their original sealed pouches until ready to use. Keep all forms of this medication away from heat, moisture, and light. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used patches by folding them sticky side together and placing them in the trash — away from children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking rivastigmine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Avoid applying the patch to skin that is red, irritated, or broken. Do not expose the patch to external heat sources like heating pads, electric blankets, or saunas, as this can increase the amount of drug absorbed into your body. Avoid suddenly stopping this medication without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; unusual weight loss; slow or irregular heartbeat; fainting or seizures; black or bloody stools; severe stomach pain; difficulty urinating; muscle weakness; worsening confusion or behavior changes; signs of skin irritation from the patch (severe redness, swelling, or blistering that spreads beyond the patch area); or signs of allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face, or trouble breathing.
when_it_works: Rivastigmine does not work overnight. It may take several weeks to months before you or your family notice improvement in memory or daily activities. Some people may not notice a big change, but the medication may be slowing the worsening of symptoms. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not notice immediate effects.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like nausea, vomiting, and dizziness — take with food and report side effects promptly. Patients with kidney or liver problems may need dose adjustments — inform your doctor of any organ problems. Patients with a history of stomach ulcers, heart rhythm problems, asthma, or seizures should use this medication with caution and inform their doctor. It is not known if rivastigmine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding — talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
